limitations: Three public document packages, not held-out or independent source families. FTA and FEMA share federal Uniform Guidance dependencies.
Selected outputs cover narrow decision slices; reading the whole source does not establish whole-document semantic recall.
The test designer is automated and knows these sources. Expectations are assistant drafts, not independently adjudicated human gold.
No provider output had been observed when these designs and expectations were prepared.
Current-law validity is outside scope: compare interpretation of exact archived editions, including dated thresholds.
Output predicates consume supplied procedural facts; no independent classification of evidence quality or legal facts is tested.
Twelve scenarios per task are a deliberately bounded diagnostic set, not exhaustive branch or semantic coverage.
FEMA other-work classification remains unknown rather than importing external-law interpretation of the labor/construction wording.

FTA effective thresholds are supplied case facts that vary across cases. Their legal establishment is outside the generation task; the model must compare fields without treating them as fixed general-law constants.
